title: SAP Workforce - My Second Brain (powered by MCC - CPR) - Download SAP Joule Skill - Set-Up Guide
author: alexanderbund
text:
Zero Fabrication — no possibility calculations applied. 
 Standard AI models generate answers by calculating the most statistically probable next token across billions of training examples. That means they can produce plausible-sounding content that is factually wrong — hallucinations that look indistinguishable from real expertise. 
 Your Second Brain operates on a different principle: the AI only works with content you have explicitly captured and stored in your vault . It retrieves, synthesizes, and surfaces your own knowledge. It does not invent what it does not find. 
 Every SAP Note reference comes from a Note you distilled. 
 Every root-cause pattern comes from a case you documented. 
 Every escalation insight comes from a newsletter you processed. 
 If it is not in your vault, the AI says so — instead of filling the gap with a confident fabrication. 
 This is the difference between a personal knowledge engine and a generic chatbot. 
 The Deeper Reason 
 The real answer isn't any single feature. It's that your Second Brain aligns with how expert performance actually works. 
 Experts aren't faster because they think faster — they're faster because they recognize patterns from prior experience and retrieve relevant context instantly. 
 Your vault is a pattern library that grows with every case, every newsletter, every escalation. It makes the implicit explicit and the short lasting durable. 
 A year from now, a new MCC engineer could open your customer case series and understand, in 30 minutes, a cascade failure pattern that took you days of live analysis to uncover. 
 That's the compounding return.

title: Co-Teaching Across the Globe? Exploring the Potential of COIL Projects
author: UtaMathis
text:
What happens when students and instructors from different countries come together in a shared virtual classroom? In this article, I share my experience with a Collaborative Online International Learning (COIL) project that connected students across continents in a Business Process Management course. 
 Through a series of joint sessions on process management, BPMN, and change management, students collaborated in international teams, exchanged perspectives, and experienced firsthand how cultural and educational differences can enrich learning. title: What makes process management so valuable? Making interface problems tangible
author: UtaMathis
text:
Understanding end-to-end processes is one thing. Experiencing the challenges that arise between departments is another. In this article, I share a hands-on teaching approach that helps students move beyond theory by simulating real-world business processes in SAP. By taking on different departmental roles and working together under time pressure, students experience firsthand how communication gaps, bottlenecks, and interface issues impact business performance. The result is a powerful learning experience that makes the value of process management tangible, memorable, and highly relevant for future professionals. 
 --> Discover how a simple yet engaging SAP simulation can transform abstract process management concepts into practical insights and inspire meaningful classroom discussions.

title: How to set up external documents via API for Singapore eInvoices?
author: Jing_Jing1
text:
You have an external system — a third-party ERP, a legacy billing platform, or even an SAP system not yet integrated with SAP Document and Reporting Compliance — that generates electronic invoices in Singapore. You need to submit these invoices to the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) or send them to customers via the InvoiceNow/Peppol network, all through SAP Document and Reporting Compliance. The question is: how do you bridge these two worlds?SAP Document and Reporting Compliance now supports External Documents for Singapore. Your external system can upload invoice XML files into SAP DRC using the gco_external REST API, and SAP DRC handles the compliance submission end-to-end. In this blog, I'll walk you through the setup steps — from SAP Note implementation to system configuration, testing, and monitoring. 
 Get to know about Singapore GST InvoiceNow requirement, and Singapore Peppol eInvoice (InvoiceNow). please check the blog 
 GST InvoiceNow - submission of invoice data to Singapore Tax Authority 
 SAP Document and Reporting Compliance for Singapore Peppol eInvoices (InvoiceNow) 

 Supported Scenarios 
 The following Singapore e-invoicing scenarios are supported through External Documents: 

 Scenario 
 Description 

 1A — Peppol Customer Invoice 
 Send a Peppol customer invoice to a customer or IRAS via InvoiceNow / Peppol Network 

 1B — Peppol Supplier Invoice to IRAS 
 Submit a Peppol supplier invoice to IRAS 

 2A/2B — Non-Peppol Customer Invoice to IRAS 
 Submit a customer invoice (non-Peppol) to IRAS 

 3A/3B — Non-Peppol Supplier Invoice to IRAS 
 Submit a supplier invoice (non-Peppol) to IRAS 
 Note: For detailed XML sample files for all four scenarios, refer to SAP Note 3840047 — Electronic Invoice Processing for Singapore: Preparation of External Documents XML Files . 

 Prerequisites 
 Before starting, ensure the following are in place: 
 SAP S/4HANA On-Premise ( S4CORE 102 or higher) or SAP ERP ( SAP_APPL 606, 617, or 618 ) 
 You have implemented Singapore DRC solution Notes. 
 SSL/TLS is configured on your SAP system 
 Your external system can call REST APIs 

 Part 1: SAP Note Implementation 
 SAP provides two separate SAP Notes for the Singapore External Documents feature, covering different submission scenarios. Implement the one(s) relevant to your business requirements. 

 SAP Note 
 Scenario 

 3752090 
 Submitting eInvoices to IRAS 

 3776506 
 Sending Peppol eInvoices to customers via InvoiceNow 
 Step 1: Implement SAP Note 3752090 (Submission to IRAS) 
 Go to transaction SNOTE . Download and implement SAP Note 3752090 . 
 Step 2: Activate BC Set EDOC_SG_C5_FACTORY_EXT_V3 
 After implementing the SAP Note, activate the Business Configuration Set that registers the Singapore-specific factory class for External Documents. Go to transaction SCPR20 . In the BC Set field, enter EDOC_SG_C5_FACTORY_EXT_V3. Activate it! Note: The Expert Mode flag is required. Without it, the factory class will not be registered correctly for Singapore. 

 Step 3: Implement SAP Note 3776506 (Peppol Submission to Customers) 
 Go to transaction SNOTE . Download and implement SAP Note 3776506 . 

 Part 2: System Configuration 
 All configuration below is done via transaction SM30 (Table View Maintenance). 
 Step 1: Define External Document Systems - Register your external system as a logical system in SAP. Enter view V_TBDLS . Create a new entry and save. 
 Logical System : A unique identifier for your external system (e.g., QKVCLNT440). 
 Name : A meaningful description. 

 Step 2: Maintain External Document Organizational Unit - Define the organizational unit within your external system that issues invoices. Enter view GCOV_EXT_ORGUNIT . Create a new entry and save. 
 External Document Org. Unit : An identifier for the external organizational unit. 
 External Document Org. Unit Description : A meaningful description. 

 Step 3: Assign External System and Org Unit to Company Code - Link the external system and org unit to the relevant SAP company code. Enter view GCOV_EXT_ORGCCOD. Create a new entry and save. 

 Step 4: Assign Process Status to External Document Status - Map external document statuses to SAP eDocument process statuses. Enter view EDOPROCEXTSTATV . Create new entries based on your requirements and save. 

 Step 5: Verify Factory Class Registration（Only required when you submit e Invoices to IRAS） Confirm that the Singapore factory class has been registered (this should already be in place after activating the BC Set in Step 2). Enter view EDOEXTAPIFACTV . Confirm that an entry exists for country SG (Singapore) with the correct factory class name. 

 eDoc. Process 
 Factory Class 
 Scenario 

 SGC5INV 
 CL_EDOC_EXT_DOC_API_SG_C5 
 Invoice submission to IRAS (C5) 

 Step 6: Activate EXT_DOC Source Type per Company Code Activate the EXT_DOC source type for each relevant company code. Without this step, the eDocument framework will reject all external documents. Enter view EDOCOMPANYACTIV . Find the entry for your Singapore company code (e.g., SG01). Ensure the Active checkbox is checked for source type EXT_DOC . 

 Part 3: API for External Documents 
 For a detailed description of the API calls, please refer to the SAP Help Portal. In this blog, I will share an example of calling the Create External Document API using Bruno. 
 Payload: {

 "logicalSystemID": "QKVCLNT440",

 "countryRegion": "SG",

 "externalDocuments": [

 {

 "externalOrgUnit": "SG_C5_TEST_ORG_UNIT",

 "externalDocumentType": "CUSTOMER_INVOICE",

 "externalDocumentSubType": "B2B",

 "externalDocumentKey": "EXTDOCAZ2026102801",

 "contentParts": [

 {

 "partType": "main",

 "partID": "PART1A"

 }

 ]

 }

 ]

} 
 Send request 

 Check in Transaction EDOC_COCKPIT or Manage Electronic Documents Fiori App 

 Note: Different externalDocumentType and externalDocumentSubType are required for different scenarios as below. 

 Scenario 
 externalDocumentType 
 externalDocumentSubType 

 1A — Peppol Customer Invoice 
 CUSTOMER_INVOICE 
 B2B 

 2A/2B — Non-Peppol Customer Invoice to IRAS 
 CUSTOMER_INVOICE 
 B2B_EMAIL 

 1B — Peppol Supplier Invoice to IRAS 
 SUPPLIER_INVOICE 
 B2B 

 3A/3B — Non-Peppol Supplier Invoice to IRAS 
 SUPPLIER_INVOICE 
 B2B_EMAIL 

 Part 4: Monitoring in SAP 
 After submission, you can track the document's processing lifecycle in SAP through two options. 
 Option 1: eDocument Cockpit (Transaction EDOC_COCKPIT) 
 Run transaction EDOC_COCKPIT . 
 Filter by country SG to find your Singapore external documents. 
 Review the processing status. Double-click a document to see details, AIF messages, and the raw XML payload. 
 Option 2: Manage Electronic Documents (Fiori App) 
 Open the Manage Electronic Documents SAP Fiori app. 
 Filter by country Singapore . 
 Review statuses, drill into individual documents, and trigger resubmissions if needed. 

 Summary 
 Here's what you've configured end-to-end: 
 SAP Note 3752090 implemented ( IRAS submission ),BC Set EDOC_SG_C5_FACTORY_EXT_V3 activated/ SAP Note 3776506 implemented ( Peppol submission to customers ) 
 External system registered as logical system, org unit defined, and assigned to company code 
 Status mapping and factory class verified 
 bgRFC destination, HTTP service, SSL, certificate mapping, and AIF all enabled 
 External system ready to POST UBL XML invoices to SAP and have them submitted to IRAS or customers via InvoiceNow/Peppol 
 I hope this blog post was useful for you! If you have questions or run into issues during your setup, feel free to leave a comment below. 
 Related Resources 
 SAP Note 3752090 — Electronic Invoice Processing for Singapore: Support for External Documents 
 SAP Note 3840047 — Electronic Invoice Processing for Singapore: Preparation of External Documents XML Files 
 SAP Note 3776506 — Electronic Invoice Processing for Singapore: New API-Based Approach for Submitting Electronic Invoices Created in External Systems 
 SAP Help Portal: Updates to Submitting Electronic Invoices Created in External Systems 
 IMDA InvoiceNow Technical Playbook: https://www.imda.gov.sg/how-we-can-help/nationwide-e-invoicing-framework/invoicenow-technical-playbook

title: What's New in SAP Integrated Product Development: Sep'26 Update
author: SreelakshmiPV
text:
What’s New for SAP Integrated Product Development 
 Welcome to the September 2026 blog! This update introduces powerful enhancements designed to accelerate innovation, strengthen collaboration, and improve efficiency across the product lifecycle. With expanded engineering capabilities and deeper integration with SAP and partner solutions, it further enhances how teams work together—from concept through manufacturing and beyond. 
 Change Management 
 Visualize Problem Report and Change Process Status Progress 
 You can now visualize the status network in the Progress tab of the Manage Problem Reports and Manage Change Processes apps. The graphical view provides a clear overview of the workflow, highlighting completed, current, and upcoming statuses. It also dynamically displays all available status transitions, making it easier to track progress and understand the workflow at a glance. 

 [Shows an overview of the changes and UI, as outlined in the text.] 
 To learn more about the feature, see Progress in Change Processes , Progress in Problem Reports . 
 Maintain Change Request Relevance for Design Item and Document Objects 
 You can now maintain additional Change Request Relevance values for Design Item and Document objects. The available options include New Version, Change, and Not Relevant , providing greater flexibility in defining how these objects are handled within a Change Request process. 

 [Shows an overview of the changes and UI, as outlined in the text.] 
 To learn more about the feature, see Change Request . 
 Add Document Business Objects to Change Management Apps 
 You can now add the Document business object across several Change Management apps, extending document support within change processes. This includes the Reference Item section in the Manage Problem Reports app, the Change Request section in the Manage Change Processes app, and the Object Types section in the Configure Change Process Types app. These enhancements provide greater flexibility in managing documents throughout the change management lifecycle. 

 [Shows an overview of the changes and UI, as outlined in the text.] 
 To learn more about the feature, see Change Request , Reference Item , Object Types . 
 Configure Workflow-Based Email Notifications 
 You can now integrate SAP Build Process Automation with Change Management to configure automated email notifications for processors whenever the status of their assigned change processes or problem reports changes. This integration helps keep processors informed of important status updates, improving visibility and streamlining change management workflows. 

 Collaboration 
 Linking Change Processes as Standard Reference Objects 
 You can now add Change Processes as standard reference objects directly from the My Collaborations app. This enhancement allows you to manage change-related activities with internal and external stakeholders within a collaboration, while ensuring end-to-end traceability between change processes and collaborative tasks. This enables better coordination and visibility throughout the change management lifecycle. 

 [Shows an overview of the changes and UI, as outlined in the text.] 
 To learn more about the feature, see Reference Objects . 
 Export Collaboration List Data to Excel 
 You can now export the complete Collaboration List page data to Excel directly from the My Collaborations app using a dedicated UI button. The export includes all attributes displayed on the list page and covers only the collaborations you are authorized to access. This enhancement makes it easier to perform offline analysis, share reports, and leverage collaboration data in external reporting tools. 

 [Shows an overview of the changes and UI, as outlined in the text.] 
 To learn more about the feature, see Working with Collaborations . 
 Common Functions 
 New SAP-Defined Link Types tab 
 You can now access a new SAP-Defined Link Types tab in the Configure Link Types screen, alongside the existing customer-defined link types. This tab provides a read-only view of predefined link types delivered by SAP, offering greater transparency into system-defined relationships. Customers can continue to create and manage their own link types, while SAP-defined link types support predefined business processes and are seamlessly handled at runtime. 

 Formulation 
 Specification Price as a new price source for Estimated Price calculations 
 You can now use Specification Price as a new price source for Estimated Price calculations in SAP IPD. 
 In the Configure Recipe Calculations app, administrators can select Specification Price as the price source and define the new Attribute for Unit Price and Attribute for Price Unit fields to specify where the system retrieves pricing information from the specifications assigned to formula items. 
 In the Manage Recipes app, product developers can now use Specification Price when viewing Estimated Price calculation results. 
 This enhancement provides greater flexibility in managing recipe cost calculations by allowing price information to be sourced directly from product specifications. 

 [Shows an overview of the changes and UI, as outlined in the text.] 
 To learn more about the feature, see Configuring Recipe Calculations , Checking Recipe Calculations . 
 More Information / Additional Links 
 Also, check out our What’s New document for regular updates! 
 To learn more about the features of SAP Integrated Product Development, visit the SAP Supply Chain Management Enablement Hub. 
 You are invited to join the PLM Experts Forum group on LinkedIn. 
 By the way, do you know how to provide feedback for SAP Integrated Product Development? Watch this video to find out how and send your feedback directly from the application. We always look forward to hearing from you.

title: Why You Should Migrate Cost Center Groups to Global Hierarchies
author: BellaZhang
text:
In an earlier release of SAP S4/HANA Cloud Public Edition, the Manage Global Hierarchies (ID: F2918) was introduced as a central place for maintaining various hierarchy types, including cost center hierarchies. One of its key purposes is to replace the legacy Manage Cost Center Groups ap p (ID: F1024) . 
 We strongly recommend migrating your cost center groups to Manage Global Hierarchies to take advantage of its enhanced capabilities, ensure business continuity, and future-proof your processes. 
 In this blog, we’ll explore the benefits of the new app, compare it with the classic app, and guide you through the migration process. 
 The Traditional Way: Manage Cost Center Groups 
 For years, cost center groups were created and edited in the classic app Manage Cost Center Groups . Cost center standard hierarchy could also be edited there. 
 The following graphic provides an overview of the app user interface: 

 To use a cost center group in reporting, the following steps are required after creating or editing the group: 
 Step 1: Mark the hierarchy as report-relevant 
 Open the Set Report Relevancy app (ID: F5295) and mark the hierarchy as report-relevant. 
 Step 2: Replicate the hierarchy 
 Use the Replicate Runtime Hierarchy (ID: F1478) app to replicate set-based hierarchies to back-end database tables. If this replication is not performed, then these hierarchies cannot be used in reporting. 

 For more information, refer to the following documentation on the SAP Help Portal: 
 Manage Cost Center Groups (Deprecated) 
 Set Report Relevancy 
 Replicate Runtime Hierarchy 
 The New Way: Manage Global Hierarchies 
 The Manage Global Hierarchies app introduced in a recent release, modernizes cost center hierarchy maintenance. Aside from viewing, creating, and editing cost center hierarchies as in the classic app, the new app enables you to quickly create hierarchies by importing or copying from existing hierarchies in the event of structure changes or changing reporting needs. Additionally, you can check change logs and maintain node texts in multiple languages for applicable hierarchy types. 
 Key Features 
 View and filter existing hierarchies by criteria such as hierarchy type, status, and validity timeframe 
 Create, copy, edit hierarchies, and manage their validity timeframes 
 Activate or deactivate hierarchies for runtime use 
 Export, edit, and import hierarchies via a spreadsheet 
 Import hierarchies created with compatible applications 
 View change logs of applicable hierarchy types 
 Maintain node texts in multiple languages for applicable hierarchy types 
 A fter being activated, hierarchies can be consumed in all analytical reports 
 Reuse Hierarchies in Group-Related Apps 
 The following graphic provides an overview of the app user interface: 
 For more information, refer to Manage Global Hierarchies on the SAP Help Portal. 
 Why Migrate? 
 Compared with the Manage Cost Center Groups app, which is used to maintain set-based groups, Manage Global Hierarchies provides a unified solution for managing various hierarchy types within a single application. In addition, thanks to the SAP Fiori UI technology, hierarchies can be exported to, edited in, and imported from spreadsheets, significantly improving maintenance efficiency. Furthermore, the global hierarchy framework simplifies the consumption of hierarchies across analytical applications and reports, enabling more consistent and seamless reporting experiences. 
 We strongly recommend using the new Manage Global Hierarchies app to maintain cost centers. Rest assured, existing cost center groups created in the classic app can be seamlessly migrated to the global hierarchies framework. We encourage you to do the migration as soon as possible for the following reasons: 
 The new app provides more robust functionality and greater flexibility to meet your business needs that are unavailable in the classic app. 
 The classic app is planned to be deprecated in the future. 
 New features are only delivered to the new app. 
 For more information, refer to Set-Based Groups versus Global Hierarchies. 
 How to Migrate: Step-by-Step 
 Migrating your existing cost center groups is simple and efficient. Follow the steps below using the Migrate Set-Based Groups to Global Hierarchies app (ID: F6228) . 
 1. Open the app , choose Hierarchy Type 0101 (Cost Center Group). 

 2. Select the old hierarchy of the cost center group you’d like to migrate, and choose the Migrate button. Take 8765 as an example. 

 3. In the migration details page, choose Migrate . 

 4. You will then be navigated to the page below, which confirms that the hierarchy has been migrated to the Manage Global Hierarchies app. 

 5. To confirm the migration, open the Manage Global Hierarchies app and check the details of 8765 . 

 6. Repeat the steps above to migrate all cost center groups. 

 After completing the migration, click the Mark as Completed button in the aforementioned migration app to finalize the process and confirm that the cost center type has been successfully and fully migrated. 
 For more information, refer to the following documentation: How to Migrate Cost Center Groups to Global Hierarchies 
 Special Case: Cost Center Standard Hierarchy 
 Among all cost center hierarchies, the Cost Center Standard Hierarchy (Hierarchy ID 1) has special behavior: 
 • Hierarchy ID 1 is reserved for the standard hierarchy. All cost centers are automatically assigned to this hierarchy upon creation. 
 • The Standard Hierarchy Node field in the Manage Cost Centers app is bidirectionally synchronized with the structure maintained in Manage Global Hierarchies . 
 • Because all cost centers are automatically assigned upon creation, the Unassigned tab is always empty for Hierarchy ID 1. 
 Note: Before activating cost center standard hierarchy 1, ensure that all cost centers have been assigned to it. Failure to do so will prevent the activation of the standard hierarchy. If you encounter this issue, check the Unassigned tab. If there are any cost centers listed, assign them to the standard hierarchy. 
 For more information, see Cost Center Standard Hierarchies on the SAP Help Portal. 
 Final Thoughts 
 The Manage Global Hierarchies app offers enhanced functionality and eliminates the need for separate report relevancy and replication steps before cost center hierarchies can be used for reporting. As the Manage Cost Center Groups app has been deprecated, migrating your cost center groups to Manage Global Hierarchies helps ensure business continuity while enabling you to take advantage of its new capabilities. We hope this blog has helped you better understand the transition process. If you have any questions or need further assistance, feel free to leave a comment below.

title: MB26 can't create outbound deliveries for serialized materials on maintenance order reservations
author: AAkash1
text:
Hi experts, 
 We're on SAP S/4HANA 2023 FPS01 with embedded EWM and PM–EWM integration. All storage locations for maintenance order components are EWM-managed. 
 Requirement When a maintenance order is released, an outbound delivery should be created automatically for its component reservations. The warehouse worker then picks and posts goods issue in EWM as usual. Only the delivery creation step needs to be automated. 
 Our plan Schedule MB26 as a background job to create the deliveries, with EWM capturing the serial number during picking. 
 The problem For serialized materials, MB26 stops with a hard error before any delivery is created: 
 Material 100045 requires serial numbers 
 KBA 1767555 says MB26 doesn't support serial numbers. It suggests using MIGO or excluding serialized materials in MB26 (Note 630888). MIGO is a dialog transaction, so it doesn't meet the automation requirement. 
 Serial number setup: 
 S/4 serial number profile ZSP1: MMSL = 03 (obligatory), SDLS = 03 (obligatory) 
 EWM serial number requirement: warehouse number level 
 Questions 
 Is there a standard SAP way to create outbound deliveries automatically for maintenance order reservations with serialized materials on EWM-managed storage locations? 
 If MMSL is set to optional (02) in the S/4 profile, will MB26 create the delivery and leave serial number capture to EWM? Have you seen any side effects? 
 How have others handled this scenario in S/4HANA with EWM?

title: 如何在 SAP Cloud ERP 中为迁移对象添加字段
author: Vincent_Zhu
text:
在将数据迁移到 SAP S/4HANA Cloud 的过程中，标准迁移对象有时无法完全覆盖企业的个性化需求——例如，某些字段并未默认包含在 SAP S/4HANA Migration Cockpit 的 XML 或 CSV 模板中。 此时，可以借助 「Model Your Migration」 （SAP S/4HANA Migration Object Modeler）应用，手动将所需字段添加到迁移对象中。 本文将以 供应商（Supplier） 对象为例，带您一步步完成操作。 ⚠️ 注意： 本文内容仅适用于使用 「通过暂存表迁移数据（Migrate Data Using Staging Tables）」 方式的场景。 
 前提条件 
 具有访问 SAP Fiori 应用「Model Your Migration Objects」的权限 
 已分配所需角色： SAP_BR_ADMINISTRATOR 
 使用的迁移方式为「通过暂存表迁移数据（Migrate Data Using Staging Tables）」 
 确认您希望添加的字段已被允许使用（请参阅对应 SAP Note，例如 SAP Note 3019787 中关于 Supplier 的说明）。 本示例中，我们将把字段 CONTACTALLOWANCECTRCENBP 添加到供应商迁移对象。 
 所有支持的迁移对象汇总说明，请参阅 SAP Note 2999428 。 
 操作步骤：以供应商迁移对象为例 
 目标：将字段 CONTACTALLOWANCECTRCENBP 添加到供应商（Supplier）迁移对象中。 
 1. 打开 Migration Object Modeler 应用 
 启动 SAP Fiori 应用「Model Your Migration Objects」，并进入您的迁移项目。 
 首次打开时，系统会提示：该应用仅支持查看和编辑使用「通过暂存表迁移数据」方式的迁移项目和对象。 如需查看使用「直接从 SAP 系统迁移数据（Migrate Data Directly from SAP system）」方式的对象，请通过「实施活动（Implementation Activities）」应用访问 SAP S/4HANA Migration Object Modeler。 

 2. 找到供应商迁移对象 
 展开迁移对象节点，查看所有对象列表，然后双击「 Supplier（供应商） 」将其打开。 

 3. 查看源结构（Source Structures） 
 双击「 Source Structures 」。 如果界面上看不到技术名称，请点击 Settings（设置） 并开启技术名称显示。 

 4. 切换至编辑模式 
 将应用切换至 Edit（编辑） 模式，以允许对迁移对象进行修改。 

 5. 添加新字段 
 选择相关的源结构，点击「 Add Field（添加字段） 」。 输入新字段的详细信息（例如 ZZ_NEW_FIELD ）；系统会将其标记为自定义字段。 
 在本示例中，我们需要添加字段 CONTACTALLOWANCECTRCENBP 。 

 6. 保存更改 
 保存您的输入。如有需要，可使用「 Full Screen on/off 」按钮切换视图。 

 7. 映射新字段（Field Mapping） 
 双击「 Field Mapping 」（确认仍处于编辑模式）。 在源结构中搜索您刚添加的字段，以及目标侧的对应字段（如 CONTACTALLOWANCECTRCENBP ）。 
 将源字段拖拽到目标字段上完成映射，或者右键点击并选择「 Assign Rule（分配规则） 」。 

 8. 验证并保存映射 
 仔细检查映射关系是否正确，然后保存更改。 

 9. 同步结构（Synchronize Structures） 
 执行结构同步，以使您的更改生效。确认弹出的提示框，然后退出应用。 

 10. 在 SAP S/4HANA Migration Cockpit 中验证 
 返回「 Migrate Your Data – Migration Cockpit 」，检查您的迁移项目，查看暂存表状态。 
 如果表状态显示为 「Adjustment Required」 ，请选中该表并点击「 Adjust Structure 」。 
 如果在 Model Your Migration 应用中已完成同步，状态应直接显示为 「OK」 。 

 11. 在模板文件中确认字段 
 新添加的字段现在将出现在迁移对象对应的 XML 模板文件中，可供数据填充使用。 

 补充说明 
 重置迁移对象： 如有需要，可将迁移对象重置为 SAP 原始模板版本。注意：此操作会移除所有自定义更改。 
 更新迁移对象： SAP 会定期更新迁移对象。当系统提示更新时，建议及时更新，以确保与最新版本的兼容性。 
 收藏夹功能： 可将常用的迁移项目或对象添加至收藏夹，方便快速访问（每类最多支持 10 个）。 
 参考资料 
 SAP Note 3019787 – 通过 Model Your Migration Objects 扩展供应商迁移对象 
 SAP Note 2999428 – 所有支持的迁移对象汇总说明 
 SAP Help Portal – 相关帮助文档 
 SAP S/4HANA Migration Object Modeler for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition（产品文档）

title: LGM Knowledge Snippet: How warehousing and transportation interact
author: BerndDittrich
text:
In SAP Logistics Management, transportation planning and warehouse execution are two sides of the same medal. A shipment cannot leave without the warehouse having picked and staged the goods - and the warehouse cannot start without transportation planning having done its part first(of course, depending on the process you are in). The two disciplines are deeply intertwined: transportation planning determines the carrier and the departure schedule, warehouse execution makes the goods physically ready, and the two services exchange precise signals at every milestone that matters. 
 This post walks through those signals - per Shipping Process. For each process: what triggers warehouse start, when the Pickup/Delivery Document (PDD) gets linked, and what happens at Staging Completed when the warehouse processing is completed. 
 LTL (Less-Than-Truckload) 
 Warehouse start is triggered as soon as the carrier is determined on the Transportation Request - no carrier confirmation is needed. If consolidation is used, the Consignment consolidation must also be finalized first followed by the carrier determination for the consignment. Once the carrier is determined, the items are ready for warehouse processing and handed over. 
 At Staging Completed: 
 If packing into Handling Units was done (which may be enforced by the HU mandatory setting in the processing variant), Staging Completed triggers creation of Package Transportation Requests from the HU structure, which adds the HU level for the TR and consignment(in case of consolidation scenarios, where the consignment is created already). 
 The PDD is not yet linked when warehouse work begins. At Staging Completed, the system searches for an open PDD matching the carrier, shipping point, and planned departure time and links it to the TR. If no match is found, the TR enters an error state requiring manual resolution (see the dedicated post on TR-PDD linking timing ). 

 Direct LTL 
 The bar is higher: the carrier must actively confirm the Consignment before the warehouse can start. That confirmation also triggers the creation of the PDD based on the carrier confirmation, which is linked to the TR immediately. This means the warehouse knows the carrier and planned departure from the very first step. 
 At Staging Completed, if packing was required, Package Transportation Requests are created from the HU structure which also updates the consignment and PDD items are also updated to package level. Because the PDD already exists, no search is needed - the update is direct. 

 FTL (Full Truck Load) 
 The subcontracting document in FTL is a Freight Order, not a Consignment. Once the Freight Order is confirmed by the carrier, the included Transportation Requests are released for warehouse processing and planned PDDs are created. The pattern is otherwise identical to Direct LTL: the PDD is known before the warehouse starts, and Staging Completed updates it to package level if packing was done. 

 Parcel 
 Like LTL, warehouse start only requires carrier determination on the TR - no Consignment exists yet. The warehouse picks and packs the goods (packing is always mandatory for Parcel). The pivotal moment is Print Label in the packing work center: this triggers Consignment creation, carrier subcontracting, and PDD creation and assignment - all in one step, before the goods reach the staging area. At Staging Completed, Package Transportation Requests are created from the HU structure and PDD items are updated to package level. 

 No Shipping / Customer Self-Pickup 
 There is no carrier, no Consignment, and no PDD. The Transportation Request is set to "Ready for Warehouse Processing" immediately on creation - no prerequisite at all. The warehouse picks and stages, and the process ends when Staging Completed is confirmed. Transportation planning receives the signal and closes out its side; no loading or carrier handoff follows. 

 What Staging Completed Always Does 
 Regardless of Shipping Process, Staging Completed is a firm boundary. Once confirmed, the HU information is final. If a correction is needed - a repack, a quantity change - staging must be explicitly reversed first. The reversal undoes everything Staging Completed triggered: Package TRs are deleted, PDD items revert to product level, and TR statuses step back. Only then can the warehouse re-work and re-confirm. 
 This is by design: Staging Completed is meant to be a clean, unambiguous signal that transportation can act on with confidence.

title: SAP TechEd 2026 Berlin: Key Innovations, AI Breakthroughs and What's New in the SAP Ecosystem
author: RanjeetKr
text:
SAP TechEd 2026 brings a new wave of enterprise innovation, putting AI agents, Joule Work, intelligent automation and connected business data at the center of the Autonomous Enterprise vision. 
 SAP TechEd 2026, held in Berlin, highlights SAP's continued commitment to transforming how businesses operate through artificial intelligence, intelligent automation and next-generation enterprise solutions. 
 This year's announcements reflect a major shift in SAP's AI strategy: moving beyond AI-powered assistance toward autonomous enterprise operations, where AI agents can understand business objectives, coordinate workflows, interact with enterprise applications and execute complex tasks with appropriate governance. 
 From enhancements to Joule Work and Joule Studio to the introduction of SAP Business AI Platform capabilities, SAP Business Data Cloud innovations and new AI models, TechEd 2026 introduces several developments that will shape the future of enterprise technology. 
 Let's explore the key announcements and innovations from SAP TechEd 2026. 
 1. Joule Work: Moving Towards Autonomous Business Operations 
 One of the biggest highlights of SAP TechEd 2026 is the continued evolution of Joule Work , SAP's AI-powered user experience designed to simplify complex business operations. 
 Joule Work enables users to describe a business goal in natural language, while AI orchestrates the required agents, applications and data across SAP and non-SAP systems to accomplish the task. 
 Some of the key enhancements include: 
 Advanced agentic thinking: Improved reasoning, planning and execution capabilities for complex business workflows. 
 Enterprise governance: Built-in audit trails, role-based permissions and human-in-the-loop checkpoints. 
 Expanded SAP Knowledge Graph integration: Better business context to help AI agents understand customer-specific processes and data. 
 Secure agent-to-agent interoperability: Improved connectivity between SAP Joule Agents and third-party AI agents through a secure gateway. 
 These developments represent an important step toward an enterprise environment where AI agents can collaborate and execute connected business processes securely. 
 2. Joule Studio: Simplifying Enterprise AI Agent Development 
 SAP is also expanding Joule Studio, making it easier for developers and business users to build, customize and manage AI agents. 
 With deeper integration into Joule Work, Joule Studio provides a shared environment for creating custom agents, extending existing Joule Agents and orchestrating workflows. 
 Key innovations include: 
 Intent-based development: Developers can describe business requirements, and Joule Studio helps identify relevant processes, APIs, data and authorizations. 
 AI agent extensions: Existing Joule Agents can be enhanced with additional instructions, APIs, MCP connections and workflow triggers. 
 n8n integration: Enables orchestration of complex workflows across SAP and non-SAP applications. 
 Agent lifecycle management: New capabilities for testing, evaluating, deploying and monitoring agents. 
 Developer flexibility: Business users can define requirements through the web experience, while developers can continue working through their preferred IDE and CLI tools. 
 SAP is also introducing pre-deployment testing and offline evaluations to help organizations validate agent behavior before production deployment. 
 The objective is to make enterprise AI development more accessible while maintaining the governance and security required for business-critical applications. 
 3. SAP Business AI Platform: Building the Foundation for Enterprise AI 
 The SAP Business AI Platform is a major part of SAP's Autonomous Enterprise strategy. 
 It brings together the capabilities required to build, contextualize, reason and govern enterprise AI solutions. 
 The platform focuses on combining business process knowledge, trusted enterprise data, AI models and governance capabilities to help organizations move beyond isolated AI pilots. 
 Key announcements include: 
 SAP Enterprise AI Gateway 
 A new centralized governance solution designed to manage AI interactions across enterprise environments. 
 It will provide: 
 Centralized authentication and authorization. 
 AI traffic routing and policy enforcement. 
 Monitoring and usage tracking. 
 Auditing and governance. 
 Secure connectivity across MCPs, APIs, AI agents and large language models. 
 Built on SAP Integration Suite, the solution aims to simplify the management of enterprise AI interactions. 
 General availability is planned for Q1 2027. 
 SAP AI Agent Hub 
 SAP is expanding AI agent governance capabilities to provide better visibility and control over SAP and third-party AI agents. 
 A new AI Governance Assistant will also help organizations assess AI systems against regulatory requirements, including the EU AI Act. 
 This will support risk classification, documentation reviews and ongoing compliance assessments. 
 4. SAP Business Data Cloud: Advancing Enterprise Data Management 
 Data remains one of the most important foundations for successful enterprise AI adoption. 
 At TechEd 2026, SAP announced new SAP Business Data Cloud capabilities designed to make enterprise data more accessible, reusable and valuable for AI and analytics. 
 Some major innovations include: 
 Expanded Lakehouse Capabilities 
 SAP is introducing native support for Apache Iceberg and a distributed SQL query engine, supported by Dremio technology. 
 These capabilities will help organizations access and process SAP and third-party data across hybrid and multi-cloud environments. 
 Potential benefits include: 
 Reduced data duplication. 
 Faster access to business insights. 
 Improved query performance. 
 Greater flexibility in data architecture. 
 Consistent governance across data environments. 
 SAP Business Data Cloud Ontology Manager 
 A new AI-assisted solution designed to help organizations create and manage domain-specific business ontologies. 
 It will enable businesses to organize relationships, rules and processes into reusable business context that AI agents can understand. 
 Enhanced SAP Knowledge Graph 
 SAP Knowledge Graph will gain support for additional SAP-managed and customer-managed data products. 
 This will help Joule and other AI agents understand company-specific business relationships and provide more relevant, context-aware responses. 
 Together, these innovations strengthen SAP's business data fabric strategy and provide a more reliable foundation for enterprise AI. 
 5. SAP HANA Cloud: AI-Powered Database Administration 
 SAP is bringing new agentic AI capabilities to SAP HANA Cloud to simplify database administration. 
 Database administrators will be able to use a conversational interface to perform tasks such as: 
 Monitoring database health. 
 Troubleshooting technical issues. 
 Optimizing SQL queries and database performance. 
 Managing database lifecycle operations. 
 Diagnosing and resolving operational issues. 
 These capabilities aim to reduce repetitive administrative work and allow database teams to focus on strategic activities. 
 General availability is planned for Q4 2026. 
 6. SAP-RPT AI Models: Smarter Predictions and Business Decisions 
 SAP is expanding its SAP-RPT family of AI models to improve the way AI understands and works with structured enterprise data. 
 Unlike traditional large language models, which primarily focus on unstructured information, tabular AI is designed to understand structured business data and support more accurate predictions. 
 Three important developments were announced: 
 SAP-RPT-TS: A time-series forecasting model designed for business scenarios such as demand forecasting. Generally available. 
 SAP-RPT-Decisions: A decision intelligence model designed to automate business decisions across workflows. General availability planned for Q4 2026. 
 SAP-RPT-2: An expanded model supporting multi-table processing, anomaly detection and structured data embeddings. General availability planned for Q1 2027. 
 SAP also announced the deployment of SAP-RPT on HPE Spaceborne Computer-2 aboard the International Space Station, demonstrating the potential of enterprise AI in edge-computing environments. 
 7. SAP Document AI: Advancing Intelligent Document Processing 
 SAP is introducing new capabilities in SAP Document AI to make document processing more intelligent and autonomous. 
 The new SAP-DOC-1 AI model is designed to extract information from different document formats without extensive upfront configuration. 
 Additional enhancements include: 
 Document splitting for processing complex, multi-page documents. 
 Custom prompting to define specific information extraction requirements. 
 Deeper integration with Joule Work. 
 Joule Studio capabilities for building document-aware agents and workflows. 
 These developments will help businesses automate document-intensive processes and reduce manual intervention. 
 General availability is planned for Q1 2027. 
 8. SAP Integration Suite: Stronger Connectivity and AI-Driven Integration 
 As enterprises adopt more AI agents, seamless connectivity between applications and systems becomes increasingly important. 
 SAP Integration Suite is receiving several enhancements to support modern integration requirements. 
 Key announcements include: 
 AI-assisted message processing error resolution. 
 AI-based detection of unusual API request payload sizes. 
 Enhanced GitHub integration for managing integration artifacts. 
 Native RosettaNet support for B2B and supply chain integration. 
 New third-party application adapters for Gmail, Google Sheets, GoToWebinar, Microsoft Excel and Salesforce Service Cloud. 
 Improved monitoring through SAP Cloud ALM. 
 These enhancements will help organizations simplify integration development, improve operational visibility and prepare their enterprise landscapes for agentic AI. 
 9. SAP Cloud ERP and RISE with SAP: AI-Driven Transformation 
 SAP is also evolving the RISE with SAP methodology to help customers adopt AI more effectively as part of their business transformation journeys. 
 The upcoming enhancements include: 
 AI-enriched implementation guidance and best practices. 
 Personalized onboarding across SAP Autonomous Suite. 
 AI readiness assessments that connect business priorities with relevant AI use cases. 
 Structured transformation road maps to help organizations measure business value. 
 The focus is on helping customers move beyond technology implementation and achieve measurable business outcomes through AI adoption. 
 General availability is planned for Q1 2027. 
 10. New SAP Certifications and Learning Opportunities 
 Alongside its technology announcements, SAP is investing in building the skills required for the next generation of enterprise AI professionals. 
 Two important learning developments include: 
 SAP Business AI Platform Solution Architect Certification 
 A new certification designed for developers, consultants, partners and solution architects. 
 It validates expertise across three major platform pillars: 
 Build. 
 Contextualize and reason. 
 Govern. 
 Joule Studio Developer Certification 
 SAP has also introduced a Joule Studio developer certification focused on building, extending and managing enterprise AI agents. 
 As part of its introductory offer, the certification is available free of charge through December 31, 2026. 
 These learning opportunities provide SAP professionals with a chance to strengthen their expertise in enterprise AI and agentic development.

title: SAP Universal ID Account Linking and Unlinking
author: barbara2020
text:
What has changed? 
 Previously, you could manually link or unlink individual S-user IDs and P-user IDs from your SAP Universal ID via SAP Account Manager. SAP Universal ID no longer serves as the Identity Provider (IdP) for authentication . Users now authenticate through SAP's standard mechanism (e.g. your S-user ID and password through Identity Authentication Service), not through the Universal ID itself. The Universal ID has effectively become an identity "wallet" for managing account associations rather than a login credential. 
 This is no longer the case. 
 From July 13, 2026, all SAP user accounts that share the same email address are automatically associated with your SAP Universal ID. The option to manually link or unlink accounts has been removed, and the Linked status column has been removed from SAP Account Manager and the Universal ID Console. 

 What does this mean for you? 
 If you have multiple IDs registered under the same email address, they will all appear automatically under your SAP Universal ID. 
 You can no longer unlink a specific S-user or P-user ID from your Universal ID manually. 

 What if you want an ID removed from your Universal ID? 
 There are three options available: 
 Option 1 — Update the email address on the ID If you do not want a specific S-user or P-user ID associated with your Universal ID, the email address on that ID can be updated to a different email address. Please contact your Super Admin to arrange this. 

 Option 2 — Delete the ID If the S-user or P-user ID is no longer required, it can be deleted. 
 S-user ID deletion can be completed by your Super Admin or by SAP support: How to find your Super administrator 
 P-user ID deletion is handled by SAP IDS- How to contact IDS: SSO@sap.com 
 Universal ID deletion is handled by CIC – How to contact CIC: https://support.sap.com/contactus 

 In both cases, confirmation will be required from the end user before any changes are made. 
 Need help? 
 If you are unsure which option is right for you, or need assistance, please reach out to your Super Admin in the first instance. 
 For further support, contact SAP through the usual support channels.

title: Stop MRP requirement transfer when sales order is in approval with supply block
author: zhaoyo
text:
Background 
 In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, the flexible approval workflow allows companies to define business rules that route sales orders to approvers before they are confirmed. A common requirement is to hold logistics activities — such as ATP confirmation, Transfer of Requirement (ToR) to MRP, and purchase requisition (PR) creation — while an order is awaiting approval. Starting a procurement run or allocating stock for an order that has not yet been approved by management wastes planning resources and can be difficult to reverse. 
 In a previous blog , I explained how to stop the Transfer of Requirement to MRP when a sales order enters the approval workflow. That blog covered the configuration approach to prevent MRP requirement transfer for orders pending approval. 
 In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2608, a new feature called Supply Block extended this capability significantly. Supply Block provides item-level control over all three logistics activities simultaneously — ATP confirmation, ToR to MRP, and PR creation — with a single configuration flag. In this blog, I will explain how to configure Supply Block to work with the approval workflow, and demonstrate the end-to-end behavior with a test scenario. 
 Business Example 
 Supply company XYZ uses the flexible approval workflow to manage high-value sales orders. When an order exceeds a certain net value threshold — or when a specific order reason is selected by the sales representative — the order is automatically routed to a sales manager for approval. The sales manager has up to 24 hours to review and either approve or reject the order. 
 The challenge: between the time the order is saved and the time the manager acts, the system is already running ATP checks, creating MRP requirements, and — for third-party or make-to-order items — generating purchase requisitions. If the manager rejects the order, these logistics activities must be manually reversed. If the manager requests changes, the items may already have been committed to stock or production. 
 Company XYZ wants all logistics activities to be completely suspended while the approval is pending, and automatically resumed as soon as the order is approved. No manual intervention should be needed to "unblock" logistics after approval. This requirement can be fulfilled through configuration alone — no BAdI implementation is needed. 
 How Supply Block Integrates with Approval Workflow 
 Before covering the configuration steps, it is important to understand how Supply Block interacts with the approval workflow. 
 When a sales order enters the approval workflow, the system evaluates the approval request reason code assigned to the order. Each reason code can be individually configured to trigger Supply Block on all items of the order. When Supply Block is triggered this way, the Supply Block Status field on each item is set to "Blocked". This stops ATP confirmation (confirmed quantity becomes zero), stops Transfer of Requirement to MRP, and prevents PR creation. 
 Critically, the Supply Block Reason field — the direct, manual supply block field on the item — remains empty. The block comes entirely from the approval workflow configuration. When the approver releases the approval request, the Supply Block Status is cleared automatically across all items, and all three logistics activities resume without any manual intervention. 
 This is different from a BAdI-driven supply block, where a custom reason code is written to the Supply Block Reason field directly. The distinction matters for troubleshooting: if an order has Supply Block Status = "Blocked" but Supply Block Reason is empty, the block source is either the approval workflow or credit management — not the BAdI. 
 Step 1: Configure the Approval Request Reasons 
 The approval workflow in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition uses approval request reason codes to classify why an order requires approval. Reason codes are customer-defined and can be created in the relevant SSCUI. 
 Go to SSCUI "Define Reasons for Approval Requests" to define a new approval request reason "ZSPB" for supply block. 

 Then go to SSCUI "Assign Reasons for Approval Requests" to assign this approval request reason to sales order, and check the indicator of "Supply Block". 

 Save the configuration and move to BAdI implementation. 
 Step 2: Implement Approval BAdI 
 You can follow SAP help to set up the flexible approval workflow for sales order. Once the flexible approval workflow is configured, you can implement the BAdI SD_APM_SET_APPROVAL_REASON to set the relevant approval request reason based on certain criteria. 
 In the BAdI implementation, evaluate the relevant business condition — net value, order reason, profit margin, or any other field available in the sales document context — and assign the appropriate reason code to salesdocapprovalreason . 
 The following example sets reason code ZSPB when the order reason is "007" (Fast Delivery). 
 * Trigger approval if the order reason is "007" 
 if salesdocument-sddocumentcategory = 'C' and salesdocument-salesdocumenttype = 'TA' and salesdocument-sddocumentreason = '007'. 
 salesdocapprovalreason = 'ZSPB'. 
 endif. 

 Save and publish the BAdI implementation. 
 Business Process Testing 
 Create a new standard sales order that meets the approval trigger condition. 

 Add the item and save the sales order. 

 Navigate to the Status and Blocks tab. The Overall Supply Block Status shows All Blocked and Approval Status shows In Approval . 

 Check the confirmed quantity on the order items. The confirmed quantity is zero — no ATP confirmation has been performed. 

 Go to app "Manage Material Coverage" and the sales order 11150 is not visible in the requirement list, which means no MRP requirement has been transferred. 
 Then approve the sales order. 

 After the approval is released, open the sales order 11150 and navigate back to the Status and Blocks tab. The Overall Supply Block Status is now Not Blocked and the Approval Status shows the approval is released. 

 The confirmed quantity is restored automatically — ATP has re-run. 

 MRP requirements are transferred, see screenshot below. 

 Connection to the Previous Blog 
 The previous blog showed how to stop Transfer of Requirement to MRP when a sales order enters the approval workflow. That approach covered one of the three logistics activities. 
 With the Supply Block feature in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2608, the same configuration mechanism now controls all three activities simultaneously: 
 Activity Previous Blog CE2608 with Supply Block 

 ATP confirmation (confirmed qty) 
 Stopped via SSCUI 102751 "Set Confirmed Quantities to Zero" 
 Stopped — same effect, no additional config 

 Transfer of Requirement to MRP 
 Workaround only — required "Fixed Date and Qty" flag set manually per item (or via API at creation) 
 Stopped automatically — no manual steps 

 Purchase Requisition creation 
 Not stopped 
 Stopped 
 If you implemented the configuration covered in the previous blog, you can extend it by enabling the "Set Supply Block" flag on the same approval request reason codes. The ToR behavior you already have is preserved, and ATP confirmation and PR creation are now also held while approval is pending. 
 Conclusion 
 The Supply Block feature in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2608 provides a straightforward, configuration-only way to hold all logistics activities while a sales order awaits approval. By enabling the Supply Block in sales order approval workflow, companies can ensure that ATP confirmation, Transfer of Requirement to MRP, and purchase requisition creation are all suspended while the order is pending — and automatically resumed upon approval, with no manual intervention needed. 
 This builds on the standard flexible approval workflow and the previously available ToR-stop capability, filling the remaining gaps in logistics gating. For companies already using the configuration from the previous blog , upgrading to CE2608 and enabling the Supply Block flag on existing reason codes is all that is needed to gain the full three-activity protection.

title: SAP Shows How to Lead with AI Governance at SAP TechEd
author: Dominik Rose
text:
This week at SAP TechEd, SAP introduced a range of solutions focused on AI governance. While the solutions address different dimensions of governance in the era of AI, they all reflect the same basic principles: 

 Build on proven business controls: You already have governance standards and practices in place. AI governance should connect to and extend these controls. 

 Adopt innovation with confidence: The approach to governance we advocate is the same publicly available and documented approach we use to develop, deploy, and govern the solutions and services we deliver. 

 Stay in control as your business grows: The controls and standards you have in place should not only promote AI adoption, but also enable you to assess costs, risks, and value as adoption increases. 

 SAP TechEd in 2026: The Autonomous Enterprise Becomes a Reality 

 Read the innovation news guide 

 Since the advent of this new world of autonomous technology, people have endeavored to identify the most impactful application of it. As the path to value realization has become clearer, a new challenge has emerged: ensuring both that AI usage does not lead to unintended and potentially harmful consequences and that this usage remains compliant with emerging regulatory regimes. 

 By adhering to the principles outlined above, SAP makes it possible accomplish both ends. More importantly, as we showed at SAP TechEd, SAP also provides the solutions necessary to govern, control, and innovate now and into the future. 

 AI governance announcements from SAP TechEd 

 Here’s what we talked about at SAP TechEd on the AI governance front. 

 True AI governance isn’t about figuring out if policies and rules have been followed after the fact; it should be about making sure governance is applied when it matters. SAP Enterprise AI Gateway ensures this kind of proactive governance by consolidating authentication, policy enforcement, and routing at runtime, while also allowing for continuous monitoring, usage tracking, and auditing. The gateway thus controls traffic across MCPs, APIs, agent-to-agent connections and LLMs. Building on SAP Integration Suite, the gateway consolidates and streamlines real-time oversight and control over AI in action. 

 As a compliment to the gateway, we also announced customer access to curated SAP Sovereign Cloud LLMs directly through SAP AI Core . This allows customers to use these LLMs in critical processes while adhering to established governance standards. What’s more, by allowing direct access on SAP Sovereign Cloud , customers can reduce both cost and complexity in AI operations. 

 Being able to provide agents with the architecture context they need to operate effectively is also essential to the control of agent behavior. At SAP TechEd, we described new features in the SAP LeanIX portfolio enabling enterprise architects to control the architecture data Joule Agents use to make and execute decisions. 

 This architecture context feature relies on a knowledge intake agent to extract relevant information from security and architecture decision documents, as well as propose connections to the SAP LeanIX knowledge graph, and submit all data for human approval before making it available to agents. 

 Finally, to support EU AI Act assessments directly in SAP AI Agent Hub , we also introduced our new AI Governance Assistant . The assistant audits and flags incomplete documentation in the agent inventory, pre-fills fields from completed assessments, identifies systems that appear high-risk but lack classification, and triggers reassessment when a fact sheet changes materially. 

 And just as the architecture context feature depends on human approval, all outputs from the AI Governance Assistant appear as drafts for legal and compliance review. 

 SAP and AI governance in depth 

 The solutions and innovations around AI governance we discussed at SAP TechEd are part of a much broader story. That story is, to a degree, historical. SAP has long played a key role in the governance of core operational and financial functions. Our approach to AI governance is built on—and a logical extension of—this legacy. 

 Of course, SAP is hardly new to this, having long ago established clear internal standards for AI governance while continuously introducing features and solutions devoted to AI governance. Among these solutions is SAP AI Agent Hub, itself an outgrowth of AI governance capabilities in SAP LeanIX. By allowing companies to quickly create and maintain a reliable inventory of agents, regardless of platform, MCP servers, and LLMs, the hub’s powerful discovery features are essential to comprehensive AI governance. 

 The other part of the story is value. While governance of AI is crucial for myriad reasons, companies invest in AI to achieve measurable business goals. As it turns out,t he observability necessary for effective governance can be leveraged and augmented to serve the purpose of performance management and evaluation. 

 With SAP Signavio agent mining capabilities, for example, you can monitor agent behavior within the context of your business processes. In this way, you can ensure agent compliance while capturing the business impact agents deliver. 

 Governance should not be an afterthought 

 The evolution of AI is not going to slow down, and neither will AI adoption. Unfortunately, while the focus here rightly falls on continuously discovering new ways to leverage AI for operational excellence and competitive advantage, this focus should not mean that governance takes a back seat. 

 Governance, on the contrary, is the key to successful AI adoption. 

 It is important to remember that governance in the era of AI is not simply a question of regulatory or corporate compliance. Because this technology involves varying degrees of autonomy, governance must be applied to the behavior of the technology itself, not just to the behavior of the humans managing it. This is one reason that we emphasize runtime enforcement of governance policies. 

 The challenge we see today, however, is that no one has yet established clear industry benchmarks and standard practices for AI governance. There also seems to be a general lack of established platforms focused on governance. 

 We say a “general lack” because, in point of fact, SAP offers precisely such a platform, one built on decades of governance expertise and experience. 

 Governance has never been an afterthought for us. And when it comes to AI governance today, as the many innovations outline here show, it is absolutely top of mind. 

 Dominik Rose is chief product officer for SAP LeanIX at SAP.
